state.case_summary:
A 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf was referred for evaluation of progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency. On presentation, temperature was 38.5 °C; heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm; respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min; jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic, especially after brief exertion. Cardiac auscultation revealed a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur and a more pronounced heartbeat on the right precordium. Lung sounds were harsh bronchovesicular. Electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia at 170 beats/min. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice, a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum, and a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum. An oblique parasternal long-axis view revealed two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, differentiated by coronary arteries from one vessel and by left and right pulmonary arteries from the other. Color-flow Doppler showed severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects. Agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein produced bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels.
